page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a single AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM, and 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Networking is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates a mix of average and weak performance profiles. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as average performance in ray tracing and image processing. However, raw CPU compute is limited, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth is also weak, registering 36.32 GB/sec for read-only and 22.69 GB/sec for write operations. For language model inference, the instance handles small 135M models at average speeds but struggles with medium 7B models, dropping to a weak 8.39 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.2xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks by bundling dedicated AMD graphics hardware with local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff lies in its CPU and memory bandwidth limitations, which restrict its utility for heavy multi-threaded CPU computing or large-scale database operations, as evidenced by its weak Redis SET performance of 7.43 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for workloads such as moderate graphics rendering, remote workstation hosting, image processing, software compilation, and light machine learning inference on smaller models.
description: Amazon Web Services g4ad.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 8 vCPUs, 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a dedicated AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. It includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and runs on the Nitro hypervisor with a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show average performance in Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation, though raw CPU compute and large-block memory bandwidth are relatively weak. Qualitatively, the instance provides a cost-effective option for graphics-intensive tasks that benefit from dedicated GPU and local NVMe storage without requiring high-end CPU performance. It is well-suited for remote workstations, moderate graphics rendering, image processing, and light machine learning inference.
